bug_semantics: Reflected XSS in the legacy Rucio WebUI: an attacker-controlled account (or another request value) is included verbatim in a Rucio exception; generate_http_error_flask serializes it as ExceptionMessage in the response body and headers; error callbacks concatenate jqXHR.responseText/ExceptionMessage into markup passed to jQuery.html(), so a victim opening a crafted authenticated WebUI URL executes attacker HTML/JavaScript in the WebUI origin. The exposed JavaScript token and non-HttpOnly session cookie amplify the result to credential theft or actions as the victim.
flaw_origin: 045193619da3087de74d77ec0f715ce57c1ed035 is the smallest commit that creates the advisory's demonstrated account_rse_usage flow. Its new account_rse_usage.js reads url_param('account'), sends it to get_account_limits/get_account_usage, and on either error executes $("#results").html('<font color="red">' + jqXHR['responseText'] + '</font>'); the new file and page do not exist in its immediate parent. Later edits retained those two sinks until the security fix. A still earlier 2014 direct-query-parameter subbar XSS family was also closed by the companion fix commit, but it does not create the advisory's specifically described 500 ExceptionMessage path and is therefore not substituted for this BIC.

reasoning: The causal unit is not the longstanding server convention of returning exception text by itself: executable behavior begins when the new WebUI page accepts an attacker-controlled account and passes the resulting response text into jQuery's HTML parser. Commit 045193619da3087de74d77ec0f715ce57c1ed035 introduces that complete, independently exploitable source-to-sink chain in one ordinary one-parent feature commit, while its direct parent lacks the page. History -L and -S reject later plotting changes, moves, and release backports as introducers. Commit 574a0b4787ab7dfd29ee0536c7da55b34e902788 is the direct closing change for the demonstrated responseText sinks; companion/backport pairs account for the three maintained release lines and exactly match the published fixed versions. Since the only permitted AI evidence is the BIC commit object and that object has a human identity and no AI marker, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
